name: Abdeel
overview: Abdeel is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Shelemiah, as noted in Jeremiah 36:26. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting a familial connection rather than a broader narrative role.
namesAndTitles: The name Abdeel means 'servant of G-d [El],' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with Hebrew naming practices. This proper name underscores a relationship of service or devotion to God, though it was not given directly by God according to the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Abdeel as the father of Shelemiah, based on the reference in Jeremiah 36:26. Beyond this paternal link, no other family relationships or descendants are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abdeel's significance in Scripture is tied to his identification as the father of Shelemiah, a figure mentioned in the context of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry. While Abdeel himself does not play a direct role in the biblical narrative, his mention helps establish the lineage and background of Shelemiah, contributing to the historical and genealogical framework within the book of Jeremiah.
